## notebooklm-mcp
NotebookLM MCP - Access NotebookLM (notebooklm.google.com).

**Auth:** If you get authentication errors, run `nlm login` via your Bash/terminal tool. This is the automated authentication method that handles everything. Only use save_auth_tokens as a fallback if the CLI fails.
**Account Switching:** To switch Google Accounts for the MCP server, run `nlm login switch <profile>` in Bash. The MCP server instantly uses the active default profile.
**Confirmation:** Tools with confirm param require user approval before setting confirm=True.
**Studio:** After creating audio/video/infographic/slides, poll studio_status for completion.

- source_add(source_type=url|text|drive|file, url=..., document_id=..., text=..., file_path=...): Add any source type
- studio_create(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Create any artifact type
- studio_revise: Revise individual slides in an existing slide deck
- download_artifact(artifact_type=audio|video|...): Download any artifact type

1	# Handoff.md - SwiftMandarin iOS Redesign
2	
3	**Last Updated (UTC):** 2026-02-23T09:30:00Z
4	**Status:** In Progress
5	**Current Focus:** Photo Translation Feature for Elementary School English Learning
6	
7	## 1) Request & Context
8	
9	- **User's request:** Rebuild the MandarinKit app as SwiftMandarin - a clean multiplatform Mandarin-English translation app with focus on iOS 26 and iPadOS 26 redesign.
10	
11	- **Key problems identified in previous version:**
12	  1. iPhone UI doesn't take up the whole screen - black bars on top/bottom
13	  2. Massive waste of space for title/settings area
14	  3. Not native-feeling on iOS
15	  4. Cross-platform code created messy conditional compilation
16	
17	- **Target devices:**
18	  - Primary: iPhone 14 Pro (iOS 26)
19	  - Secondary: iPad Pro M4 13 inch (iPadOS 26)
20	  - Tertiary: macOS 26
21	
22	- **Operational constraints:**
23	  - Single multiplatform target
24	  - iOS 26+ / iPadOS 26+ / macOS 26+ minimum deployment
25	  - Must use Apple's native Translation Framework
26	  - Must follow Apple Human Interface Guidelines (WWDC 2025)
27	  - Must adopt Liquid Glass design system
28	
29	## 2) Requirements → Acceptance Checks (Traceable)
30	
31	| Requirement | Acceptance Check | Expected Outcome | Evidence |
32	|-------------|------------------|------------------|----------|
33	| R1: Full-screen UI on iPhone | Launch on iPhone 14 Pro | Content fills entire screen, no black bars | Pending |
34	| R2: Compact, space-efficient translate view | Measure UI element sizes | No wasted space on title/settings | Pending |
35	| R3: Native iOS feel | Compare with Apple apps | Tab bar, gestures, interactions feel native | Pending |
36	| R4: Liquid Glass effects | Enable on iOS 26 | Glass effects render on controls, tab bar | Code complete |
37	| R5: Translation works | Translate "Hello" EN→ZH | Returns "你好" with pinyin | Pending runtime test |
38	| R6: Tappable Chinese words | Tap word in output | Shows popover with pinyin, definition | Code complete |
39	| R7: Vocabulary saving | Save term from popover | Term appears in Vocabulary tab | Code complete |
40	| R8: Flashcard learning | Start learning session | Cards display, ratings work | Code complete |
41	| R9: iPad sidebar/tab adaptation | Run on iPad | sidebarAdaptable shows sidebar in landscape | Code complete |
42	| R10: Photo translation feature | Take photo of English text | OCR recognizes text, shows word-by-word analysis | Code complete |
43	| R11: Word-by-word English analysis | Analyze "The cat is sleeping" | Each word shows Chinese translation and POS | Code complete |
44	| R12: Grammar point detection | Analyze sentence with grammar | Detects tenses, question forms, etc. | Code complete |
45	
46	## 3) Plan & Decomposition
47	
48	### Critical Path Narrative
49	Start with core services and models (shared across platforms), then build iOS-first UI that maximizes screen usage. The iPhone is the primary target - if it looks great on iPhone, iPad and Mac adaptations are simpler.
50	
51	### Architecture Decisions
52	
53	**Navigation Pattern:**
54	- iOS: `TabView` with `.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)` 
55	  - iPhone: Bottom tab bar (5 tabs max)
56	  - iPad landscape: Sidebar that morphs from floating tab bar
57	  - iPad portrait: Floating tab bar at top
58	- macOS: `NavigationSplitView` with sidebar
59	
60	**Tab Structure (iOS):**
61	1. **Translate** - Primary function, default tab
62	2. **Vocabulary** - Saved terms
63	3. **Learn** - Flashcards with spaced repetition
64	4. **Phrases** - Quick phrase collections
65	5. **More** - History, Statistics, Settings
66	
67	**Key iOS 26 Design Principles (from HIG research):**
68	1. **Liquid Glass** - Standard components adopt automatically; use sparingly on custom views
69	2. **Full-screen content** - Content should extend to edges with proper safe area handling
70	3. **Tab bar at bottom** - Quick access to 5 key areas
71	4. **No navigation bar titles eating space** - Use inline/large title judiciously
72	5. **Scroll edge effects** - Content scrolling under controls gets blur treatment
73	
74	## 4) To-Do & Progress Ledger
75	
76	### Completed Tasks
77	- [x] Read MandarinKit.md codebase documentation (12,627 lines) — completed
78	- [x] Research Apple HIG, Liquid Glass, TabView sidebarAdaptable — completed
79	- [x] Explore current SwiftMandarin project — completed; clean template
80	- [x] Create Models folder with SavedTerm, LearningCard, TranslationHistory, TranslationDirection — **completed**
81	- [x] Create Services folder with PinyinConverter, ChineseTextAnalyzer, SpeechService, ClipboardService — **completed**
82	- [x] Implement iOS TabView navigation structure with sidebarAdaptable — **completed**
83	- [x] Create TranslateView with full-screen design — **completed**
84	- [x] Create VocabularyView with search, sort, export — **completed**
85	- [x] Create LearnView with flashcards and spaced repetition — **completed**
86	- [x] Create PhrasesView with categories — **completed**
87	- [x] Create MoreView with History, Settings, About — **completed**
88	- [x] Apply Liquid Glass effects (.glassEffect(), .buttonStyle(.glass)) — **completed**
89	- [x] Fix all compilation errors for multiplatform support — **completed**
90	- [x] Remove template Item.swift file — **completed**
91	
92	### Remaining Tasks
93	- [ ] Test on iPhone 14 Pro simulator/device — pending
94	- [ ] Test on iPad Pro M4 simulator/device — pending
95	- [ ] Verify Translation API integration — pending
96	- [ ] Polish animations and transitions — pending
97	- [ ] App icon and branding — pending
98	- [x] Create comprehensive README.md with installation, usage, architecture, and screenshots — **completed**
99	- [x] Build macOS Release app and package distributable DMG installer — **completed**
100	
101	### Photo Translation Feature (2026-02-23)
102	- [x] Create PhotoTextRecognitionService for OCR using Vision framework — **completed**
103	- [x] Create EnglishTextAnalyzer for word analysis with NLTagger — **completed**
104	- [x] Create GrammarPoint model and knowledge base (15+ grammar points, grades 1-6) — **completed**
105	- [x] Create CameraScannerView using VisionKit DataScannerViewController (iOS only) — **completed**
106	- [x] Create EnglishRubyTextView for word-by-word display with translations — **completed**
107	- [x] Create PhotoTranslateView main interface with camera/photo/text input — **completed**
108	- [x] Update ContentView to add new Photo tab — **completed**
109	- [x] Fix duplicate FlowLayout declaration — **completed**
110	- [x] Build verification — **completed** (build succeeded)
111	
112	## 5) Findings, Decisions, Assumptions
113	
114	### Key Findings from Research
115	
116	**Liquid Glass (iOS 26):**
117	- Standard SwiftUI components (TabView, NavigationStack, toolbars) adopt Liquid Glass automatically
118	- Use `.glassEffect()` modifier sparingly on custom views
119	- Use `.buttonStyle(.glass)` for glass-styled buttons
120	- `GlassEffectContainer` for combining multiple glass effects
121	
122	**TabView sidebarAdaptable:**
123	- iOS: Bottom tab bar
124	- iPadOS: Top floating tab bar that morphs to sidebar
125	- macOS/tvOS: Always shows sidebar
126	- Limit to 5 main tabs for tab bar; use TabSection for hierarchy
127	
128	**Translation Framework:**
129	- `TranslationSession` for programmatic translation
130	- `LanguageAvailability` to check/download language packs
131	- Works offline when language packs downloaded
132	
133	### Decisions Made
134	
135	1. **Use TabView not NavigationSplitView for iOS** - Tab bar is more ergonomic for iPhone, puts navigation at thumb reach
136	2. **5 tabs: Translate, Vocabulary, Learn, Phrases, More** - Balances functionality with tab bar space
137	3. **Settings in sheet, not separate tab** - Common iOS pattern, accessed from More or gear button
138	4. **Full-width input/output areas** - No padding waste on translate view
139	5. **Pinyin always visible** - Core learning feature, not hidden behind toggle
140	6. **Use @Observable macro** - Modern Swift approach instead of ObservableObject for iOS 17+
141	7. **Platform conditionals for unavailable APIs** - #if os(iOS) for navigationBarTitleDisplayMode, insetGrouped list style
142	
143	### Assumptions
144	
145	1. User has iOS 26+ installed (Liquid Glass requires iOS 26)
146	2. Translation language packs can be downloaded on first use
147	3. UserDefaults sufficient for data persistence (used for terms, history, progress)
148	4. Apple Intelligence/FoundationModels available on target devices
149	
150	## 6) Issues, Mistakes, Recoveries

# Handoff.md - SwiftMandarin iOS Redesign

**Last Updated (UTC):** 2026-02-23T09:30:00Z
**Status:** In Progress
**Current Focus:** Photo Translation Feature for Elementary School English Learning

## 1) Request & Context

- **User's request:** Rebuild the MandarinKit app as SwiftMandarin - a clean multiplatform Mandarin-English translation app with focus on iOS 26 and iPadOS 26 redesign.

- **Key problems identified in previous version:**
  1. iPhone UI doesn't take up the whole screen - black bars on top/bottom
  2. Massive waste of space for title/settings area
  3. Not native-feeling on iOS
  4. Cross-platform code created messy conditional compilation

- **Target devices:**
  - Primary: iPhone 14 Pro (iOS 26)
  - Secondary: iPad Pro M4 13 inch (iPadOS 26)
  - Tertiary: macOS 26

- **Operational constraints:**
  - Single multiplatform target
  - iOS 26+ / iPadOS 26+ / macOS 26+ minimum deployment
  - Must use Apple's native Translation Framework
  - Must follow Apple Human Interface Guidelines (WWDC 2025)
  - Must adopt Liquid Glass design system

## 2) Requirements → Acceptance Checks (Traceable)

| Requirement | Acceptance Check | Expected Outcome | Evidence |
|-------------|------------------|------------------|----------|
| R1: Full-screen UI on iPhone | Launch on iPhone 14 Pro | Content fills entire screen, no black bars | Pending |
| R2: Compact, space-efficient translate view | Measure UI element sizes | No wasted space on title/settings | Pending |
| R3: Native iOS feel | Compare with Apple apps | Tab bar, gestures, interactions feel native | Pending |
| R4: Liquid Glass effects | Enable on iOS 26 | Glass effects render on controls, tab bar | Code complete |
| R5: Translation works | Translate "Hello" EN→ZH | Returns "你好" with pinyin | Pending runtime test |
| R6: Tappable Chinese words | Tap word in output | Shows popover with pinyin, definition | Code complete |
| R7: Vocabulary saving | Save term from popover | Term appears in Vocabulary tab | Code complete |

| R11: Word-by-word English analysis | Analyze "The cat is sleeping" | Each word shows Chinese translation and POS | Code complete |
| R12: Grammar point detection | Analyze sentence with grammar | Detects tenses, question forms, etc. | Code complete |

## 3) Plan & Decomposition

### Critical Path Narrative
Start with core services and models (shared across platforms), then build iOS-first UI that maximizes screen usage. The iPhone is the primary target - if it looks great on iPhone, iPad and Mac adaptations are simpler.

### Architecture Decisions

**Navigation Pattern:**
- iOS: `TabView` with `.tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable)` 
  - iPhone: Bottom tab bar (5 tabs max)
  - iPad landscape: Sidebar that morphs from floating tab bar
  - iPad portrait: Floating tab bar at top
- macOS: `NavigationSplitView` with sidebar

**Tab Structure (iOS):**
1. **Translate** - Primary function, default tab
2. **Vocabulary** - Saved terms
3. **Learn** - Flashcards with spaced repetition
4. **Phrases** - Quick phrase collections
5. **More** - History, Statistics, Settings

**Key iOS 26 Design Principles (from HIG research):**
1. **Liquid Glass** - Standard components adopt automatically; use sparingly on custom views
2. **Full-screen content** - Content should extend to edges with proper safe area handling
3. **Tab bar at bottom** - Quick access to 5 key areas
4. **No navigation bar titles eating space** - Use inline/large title judiciously
5. **Scroll edge effects** - Content scrolling under controls gets blur treatment

## 5) Findings, Decisions, Assumptions

### Key Findings from Research

**Liquid Glass (iOS 26):**
- Standard SwiftUI components (TabView, NavigationStack, toolbars) adopt Liquid Glass automatically
- Use `.glassEffect()` modifier sparingly on custom views
- Use `.buttonStyle(.glass)` for glass-styled buttons
- `GlassEffectContainer` for combining multiple glass effects

**TabView sidebarAdaptable:**
- iOS: Bottom tab bar
- iPadOS: Top floating tab bar that morphs to sidebar
- macOS/tvOS: Always shows sidebar
- Limit to 5 main tabs for tab bar; use TabSection for hierarchy

**Translation Framework:**
- `TranslationSession` for programmatic translation
- `LanguageAvailability` to check/download language packs
- Works offline when language packs downloaded

### Decisions Made

1. **Use TabView not NavigationSplitView for iOS** - Tab bar is more ergonomic for iPhone, puts navigation at thumb reach
2. **5 tabs: Translate, Vocabulary, Learn, Phrases, More** - Balances functionality with tab bar space
3. **Settings in sheet, not separate tab** - Common iOS pattern, accessed from More or gear button
4. **Full-width input/output areas** - No padding waste on translate view
5. **Pinyin always visible** - Core learning feature, not hidden behind toggle
6. **Use @Observable macro** - Modern Swift approach instead of ObservableObject for iOS 17+
7. **Platform conditionals for unavailable APIs** - #if os(iOS) for navigationBarTitleDisplayMode, insetGrouped list style

### Assumptions

1. User has iOS 26+ installed (Liquid Glass requires iOS 26)
2. Translation language packs can be downloaded on first use
3. UserDefaults sufficient for data persistence (used for terms, history, progress)

5	//  Photo OCR service using Apple Vision framework
6	//  Recognizes text in images for translation

8	
9	import Foundation
10	import Vision

12	
13	#if canImport(UIKit)
14	import UIKit
15	#elseif canImport(AppKit)
16	import AppKit
17	#endif

19	/// Result of text recognition from an image
20	struct RecognizedTextBlock: Identifiable, Sendable {
21	    let id = UUID()
22	    let text: String
23	    let confidence: Float
24	    let boundingBox: CGRect
25	}
26	
27	/// Combined recognition result
28	struct TextRecognitionResult: Sendable {
29	    let blocks: [RecognizedTextBlock]
30	    let fullText: String
31	    let cleanedText: String  // Text with line breaks cleaned up for sentence processing
32	    let language: String?
33	    
34	    var isEmpty: Bool { blocks.isEmpty }
35	    
36	    init(blocks: [RecognizedTextBlock]) {
37	        self.blocks = blocks
38	        self.fullText = blocks.map { $0.text }.joined(separator: "\n")
39	        self.cleanedText = TextRecognitionResult.cleanTextForSentences(blocks.map { $0.text }.joined(separator: " "))
40	        self.language = nil
41	    }
42	    
43	    /// Clean OCR text to properly join sentences split by line breaks
44	    /// This is important for textbook scanning where sentences may span multiple lines
45	    private static func cleanTextForSentences(_ text: String) -> String {
46	        var result = text
47	        
48	        // Replace multiple whitespace/newlines with single space
49	        result = result.replacingOccurrences(of: "\\s+", with: " ", options: .regularExpression)
50	        
51	        // Fix common OCR issues where sentences are split by line breaks
52	        // Pattern: lowercase letter followed by newline/space followed by lowercase letter (likely mid-sentence)
53	        // Keep line breaks after sentence-ending punctuation
54	        
55	        // First, normalize all whitespace to single spaces
56	        result = result.components(separatedBy: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
57	            .filter { !$0.isEmpty }
58	            .joined(separator: " ")
59	        
60	        // Fix hyphenated words split across lines (e.g., "com- municate" -> "communicate")
61	        result = result.replacingOccurrences(of: "- ", with: "")
62	        
63	        // Ensure proper spacing after punctuation
64	        result = result.replacingOccurrences(of: "\\.([A-Z])", with: ". $1", options: .regularExpression)
65	        result = result.replacingOccurrences(of: "\\?([A-Z])", with: "? $1", options: .regularExpression)
66	        result = result.replacingOccurrences(of: "!([A-Z])", with: "! $1", options: .regularExpression)
67	        
68	        // Clean up multiple spaces
69	        result = result.replacingOccurrences(of: "  +", with: " ", options: .regularExpression)
70	        
71	        return result.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
72	    }
73	}

75	/// Errors that can occur during text recognition
76	enum RecognitionError: LocalizedError {
77	    case invalidImage
78	    case recognitionFailed(String)
79	    case noTextFound
80	    case unsupportedPlatform
81	    
82	    var errorDescription: String? {
83	        switch self {
84	        case .invalidImage:
85	            return "无法处理图片"
86	        case .recognitionFailed(let message):
87	            return "识别失败: \(message)"
88	        case .noTextFound:

90	        case .unsupportedPlatform:

93	    }
94	}

98	@MainActor
99	final class PhotoTextRecognitionService {
100	    
101	    static let shared = PhotoTextRecognitionService()
102	    
103	    /// Current recognition state
104	    var isProcessing: Bool = false
105	    var lastError: String?
106	    var lastResult: TextRecognitionResult?
107	    
108	    private init() {}
109	    
110	    // MARK: - Public Methods
111	    
112	    /// Recognize text in a CGImage
113	    func recognizeText(in cgImage: CGImage) async throws -> TextRecognitionResult {
114	        isProcessing = true
115	        lastError = nil
116	        
117	        defer { isProcessing = false }
118	        
119	        do {
120	            let blocks = try await performRecognition(cgImage: cgImage)
121	            
122	            if blocks.isEmpty {
123	                throw RecognitionError.noTextFound
124	            }
125	            
126	            let result = TextRecognitionResult(blocks: blocks)
127	            lastResult = result
128	            return result
129	        } catch {
130	            lastError = error.localizedDescription
131	            throw error
132	        }
133	    }
134	    
135	    #if canImport(UIKit)
136	    /// Recognize text in a UIImage
137	    func recognizeText(in image: UIImage) async throws -> TextRecognitionResult {
138	        guard let cgImage = image.cgImage else {
139	            throw RecognitionError.invalidImage
140	        }
141	        return try await recognizeText(in: cgImage)
142	    }
143	    #endif
144	    
145	    #if canImport(AppKit)
146	    /// Recognize text in an NSImage
147	    func recognizeText(in image: NSImage) async throws -> TextRecognitionResult {
148	        guard let cgImage = image.cgImage(forProposedRect: nil, context: nil, hints: nil) else {
149	            throw RecognitionError.invalidImage
150	        }
151	        return try await recognizeText(in: cgImage)
152	    }
153	    #endif
154	    
155	    /// Recognize text from image data
156	    func recognizeText(from data: Data) async throws -> TextRecognitionResult {
157	        #if canImport(UIKit)
158	        guard let image = UIImage(data: data), let cgImage = image.cgImage else {
159	            throw RecognitionError.invalidImage
160	        }
161	        #elseif canImport(AppKit)
162	        guard let image = NSImage(data: data),
163	              let cgImage = image.cgImage(forProposedRect: nil, context: nil, hints: nil) else {
164	            throw RecognitionError.invalidImage
165	        }
166	        #endif
167	        
168	        return try await recognizeText(in: cgImage)
169	    }
170	    
171	    // MARK: - Private Methods
172	    
173	    private func performRecognition(cgImage: CGImage) async throws -> [RecognizedTextBlock] {
174	        try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
175	            let request = VNRecognizeTextRequest { request, error in
176	                if let error = error {
177	                    continuation.resume(throwing: RecognitionError.recognitionFailed(error.localizedDescription))
178	                    return
179	                }
180	                
181	                guard let observations = request.results as? [VNRecognizedTextObservation] else {
182	                    continuation.resume(returning: [])
183	                    return
184	                }
185	                
186	                let blocks = observations.compactMap { observation -> RecognizedTextBlock? in
187	                    // Get the top candidate for each observation
188	                    guard let candidate = observation.topCandidates(1).first else { return nil }
189	                    
190	                    return RecognizedTextBlock(
191	                        text: candidate.string,
192	                        confidence: candidate.confidence,
193	                        boundingBox: observation.boundingBox
194	                    )
195	                }
196	                
197	                continuation.resume(returning: blocks)
198	            }
199	            
200	            // Configure for accurate recognition
201	            request.recognitionLevel = .accurate
202	            
203	            // Prioritize English for textbook scanning
204	            request.recognitionLanguages = ["en-US", "en-GB", "zh-Hans", "zh-Hant"]
205	            
206	            // Enable language correction for better accuracy
207	            request.usesLanguageCorrection = true
208	            
209	            // Use revision 3 for best accuracy (iOS 16+)
210	            if #available(iOS 16.0, macOS 13.0, *) {
211	                request.revision = VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision3
212	            }
213	            
214	            let handler = VNImageRequestHandler(cgImage: cgImage, options: [:])
215	            
216	            do {
217	                try handler.perform([request])
218	            } catch {
219	                continuation.resume(throwing: RecognitionError.recognitionFailed(error.localizedDescription))
220	            }
221	        }
222	    }
223	    
224	    /// Clear the last result and error
225	    func reset() {
226	        lastResult = nil
227	        lastError = nil
228	    }
229	}

385	    ///   - pinyin: Optional pinyin for the word
386	    ///   - context: Optional sentence context

388	    func generateExplanationWithProvider(
389	        for word: String,

391	        context: String? = nil
392	    ) async throws -> WordExplanationResult {
393	        let settings = AIModelSettings.shared

396	        case .appleIntelligence:

398	        case .ollama:

404	    /// - Parameters:

407	    /// - Returns: The translated text

409	        let settings = AIModelSettings.shared
410	        
411	        switch settings.effectiveProvider {
412	        case .appleIntelligence:
413	            return try await translate(text, sourceIsChinese: sourceIsChinese)

419	    // MARK: - Ollama-Specific Methods
420	    
421	    /// Generate a word explanation using Ollama
422	    private func generateExplanationWithOllama(
423	        for word: String,
424	        pinyin: String? = nil,
425	        context: String? = nil
426	    ) async throws -> WordExplanationResult {
427	        let settings = AIModelSettings.shared
428	        
429	        guard OllamaService.shared.isConnected else {
430	            throw AIExplanationError.ollamaNotConnected
431	        }
432	        
433	        guard !settings.ollamaModel.isEmpty else {
434	            throw AIExplanationError.ollamaNoModelSelected
435	        }
436	        
437	        // Check cache first
438	        let cacheKey = "ollama_\(word)_\(pinyin ?? "")_\(context ?? "")"
439	        if let cached = explanationCache[cacheKey] {
440	            return cached
441	        }
442	        
443	        // Build prompt
444	        var prompt = "Explain the Chinese word: \(word)"
445	        if let pinyin = pinyin, !pinyin.isEmpty {
446	            prompt += " (\(pinyin))"
447	        }
448	        prompt += ". Use \"\(word)\" exactly in all example sentences."
449	        if let context = context, !context.isEmpty {
450	            prompt += " Context: \"\(context)\""
451	        }
452	        
453	        // JSON schema for structured output
454	        let schema: Ollama.Value = [
455	            "type": "object",
456	            "properties": [
457	                "definition": ["type": "string", "description": "A clear, concise definition in English (1-2 sentences)"],
458	                "partOfSpeech": ["type": "string", "description": "The part of speech (noun, verb, adjective, etc.)"],
459	                "nuances": ["type": "string", "description": "Cultural or contextual nuances, formality level"],
460	                "grammarUsage": ["type": "string", "description": "Grammatical explanation including sentence patterns"],
461	                "usageContexts": [
462	                    "type": "array",
463	                    "items": ["type": "string"],
464	                    "description": "1-3 common contexts where this word is used"
465	                ],
466	                "exampleSentences": [
467	                    "type": "array",
468	                    "items": [
469	                        "type": "object",
470	                        "properties": [
471	                            "chinese": ["type": "string", "description": "Example sentence containing the EXACT word"],
472	                            "pinyin": ["type": "string", "description": "Pinyin with tone marks (ā á ǎ à)"],
473	                            "english": ["type": "string", "description": "English translation"]
474	                        ],
475	                        "required": ["chinese", "pinyin", "english"]
476	                    ],
477	                    "description": "1-3 example sentences"
478	                ],
479	                "synonyms": [
480	                    "type": "array",
481	                    "items": [
482	                        "type": "object",
483	                        "properties": [
484	                            "chinese": ["type": "string"],
485	                            "pinyin": ["type": "string"],
486	                            "meaning": ["type": "string"],
487	                            "difference": ["type": "string", "description": "How it differs from the main word"]
488	                        ],
489	                        "required": ["chinese", "pinyin", "meaning", "difference"]
490	                    ],
491	                    "description": "1-2 similar words"
492	                ],
493	                "antonyms": [
494	                    "type": "array",
495	                    "items": [
496	                        "type": "object",
497	                        "properties": [
498	                            "chinese": ["type": "string"],
499	                            "pinyin": ["type": "string"],
500	                            "meaning": ["type": "string"],
501	                            "difference": ["type": "string"]
502	                        ],
503	                        "required": ["chinese", "pinyin", "meaning", "difference"]
504	                    ],
505	                    "description": "0-2 opposite words if applicable"
506	                ],
507	                "commonCollocations": [
508	                    "type": "array",
509	                    "items": [
510	                        "type": "object",
511	                        "properties": [
512	                            "chinese": ["type": "string", "description": "Phrase containing the word"],
513	                            "pinyin": ["type": "string"],
514	                            "english": ["type": "string"]
515	                        ],
516	                        "required": ["chinese", "pinyin", "english"]
517	                    ],
518	                    "description": "1-2 common phrases with this word"
519	                ],
520	                "learningTip": ["type": "string", "description": "Brief note on difficulty and learning tips"]
521	            ],
522	            "required": ["definition", "partOfSpeech", "nuances", "grammarUsage", "usageContexts", "exampleSentences", "synonyms", "commonCollocations", "learningTip"]
523	        ]
524	        
525	        let jsonString = try await OllamaService.shared.generateStructured(
526	            model: settings.ollamaModel,
527	            systemPrompt: ollamaSystemInstructions,
528	            userPrompt: prompt,
529	            schema: schema,
530	            enableThinking: settings.enableThinking
531	        )
532	        
533	        // Parse JSON response
534	        guard let data = jsonString.data(using: .utf8) else {
535	            throw AIExplanationError.generationFailed("Invalid UTF-8 response")
536	        }
537	        
538	        let response = try JSONDecoder().decode(OllamaWordExplanationResponse.self, from: data)
539	        let result = response.toResult(filteringFor: word)
540	        
541	        // Cache the result
542	        explanationCache[cacheKey] = result
543	        
544	        return result

547	    /// Translate text using Ollama
548	    private func translateWithOllama(_ text: String, sourceIsChinese: Bool) async throws -> String {
549	        let settings = AIModelSettings.shared
550	        
551	        guard OllamaService.shared.isConnected else {
552	            throw AIExplanationError.ollamaNotConnected
553	        }
554	        
555	        guard !settings.ollamaModel.isEmpty else {
556	            throw AIExplanationError.ollamaNoModelSelected
557	        }
558	        
559	        return try await OllamaService.shared.translate(
560	            text,
561	            sourceIsChinese: sourceIsChinese,
562	            model: settings.ollamaModel
563	        )
564	    }

566	    /// System instructions for Ollama word explanation
567	    private var ollamaSystemInstructions: String {
568	        """
569	        You are an expert Mandarin Chinese teacher helping English-speaking learners understand Chinese vocabulary.
570	        
571	        CRITICAL RULES:
572	        1. Example sentences MUST contain the EXACT word being explained - never use synonyms or variations
573	        2. Pinyin must have correct tone marks (ā á ǎ à ē é ě è ī í ǐ ì ō ó ǒ ò ū ú ǔ ù ǖ ǘ ǚ ǜ) matching each character exactly
574	        3. For multi-character words like "给予", use "给予" in examples, not just "给"
575	        4. Provide thoughtful, educational explanations that help learners understand usage patterns
576	        5. Consider register (formal/informal), regional variations, and common learner mistakes
577	        
578	        Take your time to think through each aspect carefully to provide accurate, helpful information.
579	        """
580	    }
581	}
582	
583	// MARK: - Errors
584	
585	enum AIExplanationError: LocalizedError {
586	    case unavailable(reason: String)
587	    case generationFailed(String)
588	    case ollamaNotConnected
589	    case ollamaNoModelSelected
590	    
591	    var errorDescription: String? {
592	        switch self {
593	        case .unavailable(let reason):
594	            return "AI unavailable: \(reason)"
595	        case .generationFailed(let message):
596	            return "Failed to generate explanation: \(message)"
597	        case .ollamaNotConnected:
598	            return "Ollama server is not connected. Please check that Ollama is running."
599	        case .ollamaNoModelSelected:
600	            return "No Ollama model selected. Please select a model in Settings."
601	        }
602	    }
603	}
604	
605	// MARK: - Ollama Word Explanation Response (for JSON decoding)
606	
607	/// Codable struct for parsing Ollama JSON responses for word explanations
608	struct OllamaWordExplanationResponse: Codable {
609	    let definition: String
610	    let partOfSpeech: String
611	    let nuances: String
612	    let grammarUsage: String
613	    let usageContexts: [String]
614	    let exampleSentences: [OllamaExampleSentence]
615	    let synonyms: [OllamaRelatedWord]
616	    let antonyms: [OllamaRelatedWord]?
617	    let commonCollocations: [OllamaCollocation]
618	    let learningTip: String
619	    
620	    struct OllamaExampleSentence: Codable {
621	        let chinese: String
622	        let pinyin: String
623	        let english: String
624	    }
625	    
626	    struct OllamaRelatedWord: Codable {
627	        let chinese: String
628	        let pinyin: String
629	        let meaning: String
630	        let difference: String
631	    }
632	    
633	    struct OllamaCollocation: Codable {
634	        let chinese: String
635	        let pinyin: String
636	        let english: String
637	    }
638	    
639	    /// Convert to WordExplanationResult
640	    func toResult(filteringFor word: String) -> WordExplanationResult {
641	        // Filter example sentences to only include those that contain the exact word
642	        let validExamples = exampleSentences.filter { sentence in
643	            sentence.chinese.contains(word)
644	        }
645	        
646	        // Filter collocations to only include those that contain the word
647	        let validCollocations = commonCollocations.filter { collocation in
648	            collocation.chinese.contains(word)
649	        }
650	        
651	        return WordExplanationResult(
652	            definition: definition,
653	            partOfSpeech: partOfSpeech,
654	            nuances: nuances,
655	            grammarUsage: grammarUsage,
656	            usageContexts: usageContexts,
657	            exampleSentences: validExamples.map {
658	                ExampleSentenceResult(chinese: $0.chinese, pinyin: $0.pinyin, english: $0.english)
659	            },
660	            synonyms: synonyms.map {
661	                RelatedWordResult(chinese: $0.chinese, pinyin: $0.pinyin, meaning: $0.meaning, difference: $0.difference)
662	            },
663	            antonyms: (antonyms ?? []).map {
664	                RelatedWordResult(chinese: $0.chinese, pinyin: $0.pinyin, meaning: $0.meaning, difference: $0.difference)
665	            },
666	            commonCollocations: validCollocations.map {
667	                CollocationResult(chinese: $0.chinese, pinyin: $0.pinyin, english: $0.english)
668	            },
669	            learningTip: learningTip
670	        )
671	    }
672	}

1	//
2	//  WordTranslationService.swift
3	//  SwiftMandarin
4	//
5	//  Service for translating individual words/phrases using Apple's Translation API
6	//  Provides per-word translations for word detail popovers
7	//
8	
9	import Foundation
10	import Translation
11	
12	/// Service for translating individual words using Apple's Translation API
13	@Observable
14	final class WordTranslationService {
15	    
16	    static let shared = WordTranslationService()
17	    
18	    /// Cache for translated words to avoid repeated API calls
19	    private var translationCache: [String: String] = [:]
20	    
21	    private init() {}
22	    
23	    // MARK: - Public Methods
24	    
25	    /// Translate a single word or phrase from Chinese to English
26	    /// Uses installed language packs (requires languages to be pre-downloaded)
27	    /// - Parameter word: The Chinese word/phrase to translate
28	    /// - Returns: The English translation
29	    func translateToEnglish(_ word: String) async throws -> String {
30	        // Check cache first
31	        let cacheKey = "zh-en:\(word)"
32	        if let cached = translationCache[cacheKey] {
33	            return cached
34	        }
35	        
36	        // Create translation session for Chinese to English using installed languages
37	        let session = try await TranslationSession(
38	            installedSource: Locale.Language(identifier: "zh-Hans"),
39	            target: Locale.Language(identifier: "en")
40	        )
41	        
42	        let response = try await session.translate(word)
43	        
44	        // Cache the result
45	        translationCache[cacheKey] = response.targetText
46	        
47	        return response.targetText
48	    }
49	    
50	    /// Translate a single word or phrase from English to Chinese
51	    /// Uses installed language packs (requires languages to be pre-downloaded)
52	    /// - Parameter word: The English word/phrase to translate
53	    /// - Returns: The Chinese translation
54	    func translateToChinese(_ word: String) async throws -> String {
55	        // Check cache first
56	        let cacheKey = "en-zh:\(word)"
57	        if let cached = translationCache[cacheKey] {
58	            return cached
59	        }
60	        
61	        // Create translation session for English to Chinese using installed languages
62	        let session = try await TranslationSession(
63	            installedSource: Locale.Language(identifier: "en"),
64	            target: Locale.Language(identifier: "zh-Hans")
65	        )
66	        
67	        let response = try await session.translate(word)
68	        
69	        // Cache the result
70	        translationCache[cacheKey] = response.targetText
71	        
72	        return response.targetText
73	    }
74	    
75	    /// Translate a word with automatic language detection
76	    /// - Parameters:
77	    ///   - word: The word to translate
78	    ///   - sourceIsChinese: Whether the source word is Chinese
79	    /// - Returns: The translated word in the opposite language
80	    func translate(_ word: String, sourceIsChinese: Bool) async throws -> String {
81	        if sourceIsChinese {
82	            return try await translateToEnglish(word)
83	        } else {
84	            return try await translateToChinese(word)
85	        }
86	    }
87	    
88	    /// Batch translate multiple words (more efficient for multiple lookups)
89	    /// - Parameters:
90	    ///   - words: Array of words to translate
91	    ///   - sourceIsChinese: Whether source words are Chinese
92	    /// - Returns: Dictionary mapping original words to translations
93	    func translateBatch(_ words: [String], sourceIsChinese: Bool) async throws -> [String: String] {
94	        var results: [String: String] = [:]
95	        var wordsToTranslate: [String] = []
96	        
97	        // Check cache first
98	        let cachePrefix = sourceIsChinese ? "zh-en:" : "en-zh:"
99	        for word in words {
100	            let cacheKey = "\(cachePrefix)\(word)"
101	            if let cached = translationCache[cacheKey] {
102	                results[word] = cached
103	            } else {
104	                wordsToTranslate.append(word)
105	            }
106	        }
107	        
108	        // Return early if all words were cached
109	        if wordsToTranslate.isEmpty {
110	            return results
111	        }
112	        
113	        // Create translation session using installed languages
114	        let session = try await TranslationSession(
115	            installedSource: sourceIsChinese ? Locale.Language(identifier: "zh-Hans") : Locale.Language(identifier: "en"),
116	            target: sourceIsChinese ? Locale.Language(identifier: "en") : Locale.Language(identifier: "zh-Hans")
117	        )
118	        
119	        // Create batch requests with client identifiers for matching
120	        var requests: [TranslationSession.Request] = []
121	        for (index, word) in wordsToTranslate.enumerated() {
122	            requests.append(TranslationSession.Request(
123	                sourceText: word,
124	                clientIdentifier: "\(index)"
125	            ))
126	        }
127	        
128	        // Perform batch translation
129	        let responses = try await session.translations(from: requests)
130	        
131	        // Process responses and update cache
132	        for response in responses {
133	            if let clientId = response.clientIdentifier,
134	               let index = Int(clientId),
135	               index < wordsToTranslate.count {
136	                let originalWord = wordsToTranslate[index]
137	                let translation = response.targetText
138	                
139	                results[originalWord] = translation
140	                translationCache["\(cachePrefix)\(originalWord)"] = translation
141	            }
142	        }
143	        
144	        return results
145	    }
146	    
147	    /// Clear the translation cache
148	    func clearCache() {
149	        translationCache.removeAll()
150	    }
151	    
152	    /// Get cached translation if available
153	    func getCachedTranslation(for word: String, sourceIsChinese: Bool) -> String? {
154	        let cacheKey = sourceIsChinese ? "zh-en:\(word)" : "en-zh:\(word)"
155	        return translationCache[cacheKey]
156	    }
157	}

1	//
2	//  ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift
3	//  SwiftMandarin
4	//
5	//  Chinese text analysis using Apple's Natural Language framework
6	//
7	
8	import Foundation
9	import NaturalLanguage
10	import SwiftUI
11	
12	final class ChineseTextAnalyzer {
13	    
14	    static let shared = ChineseTextAnalyzer()
15	    private init() {}
16	    
17	    // MARK: - Word Segmentation
18	    
19	    func segmentWords(_ text: String) -> [SegmentedWord] {
20	        let tokenizer = NLTokenizer(unit: .word)
21	        tokenizer.string = text
22	        tokenizer.setLanguage(.simplifiedChinese)
23	        
24	        var words: [SegmentedWord] = []
25	        
26	        tokenizer.enumerateTokens(in: text.startIndex..<text.endIndex) { range, _ in
27	            let word = String(text[range])
28	            words.append(SegmentedWord(text: word, range: range))
29	            return true
30	        }
31	        
32	        return words
33	    }
34	    
35	    func segmentWithPartsOfSpeech(_ text: String) -> [AnalyzedWord] {
36	        let tagger = NLTagger(tagSchemes: [.lexicalClass])
37	        tagger.string = text
38	        tagger.setLanguage(.simplifiedChinese, range: text.startIndex..<text.endIndex)
39	        
40	        var words: [AnalyzedWord] = []
41	        
42	        // Don't omit punctuation - we want to preserve it in the output
43	        tagger.enumerateTags(in: text.startIndex..<text.endIndex,
44	                            unit: .word,
45	                            scheme: .lexicalClass,
46	                            options: [.omitWhitespace]) { tag, range in
47	            let word = String(text[range])
48	            let partOfSpeech = tag.map { PartOfSpeech(from: $0) } ?? .unknown
49	            
50	            // Include all tokens including punctuation
51	            words.append(AnalyzedWord(text: word, range: range, partOfSpeech: partOfSpeech))
52	            return true
53	        }
54	        
55	        return words
56	    }
57	    
58	    // MARK: - Language Detection
59	    
60	    func detectLanguage(_ text: String) -> DetectedLanguage {
61	        let recognizer = NLLanguageRecognizer()
62	        recognizer.processString(text)
63	        
64	        guard let language = recognizer.dominantLanguage else {
65	            return .unknown
66	        }
67	        
68	        switch language {
69	        case .simplifiedChinese, .traditionalChinese:
70	            return .chinese
71	        case .english:
72	            return .english
73	        default:
74	            return .other(language.rawValue)
75	        }
76	    }
77	    
78	    func detectLanguageWithConfidence(_ text: String) -> (language: DetectedLanguage, confidence: Double) {
79	        let recognizer = NLLanguageRecognizer()
80	        recognizer.processString(text)
81	        
82	        let hypotheses = recognizer.languageHypotheses(withMaximum: 3)
83	        
84	        guard let dominant = recognizer.dominantLanguage,
85	              let confidence = hypotheses[dominant] else {
86	            return (.unknown, 0.0)
87	        }
88	        
89	        let detectedLanguage: DetectedLanguage
90	        switch dominant {
91	        case .simplifiedChinese, .traditionalChinese:
92	            detectedLanguage = .chinese
93	        case .english:
94	            detectedLanguage = .english
95	        default:
96	            detectedLanguage = .other(dominant.rawValue)
97	        }
98

# SwiftMandarin — Implementation Brief: OCR Language Fix, Multi-Provider AI, Photo AI Cleanup

## 1. Overall Architecture

SwiftMandarin is a cross-platform (iOS + macOS) SwiftUI Mandarin-learning app. State lives in **`@Observable @MainActor` singletons** (`.shared`) backed by **UserDefaults JSON blobs** — there is no SwiftData/CoreData in active use (`Item.swift` is a dead template stub). The five core stores (`SavedTermsStore`, `TranslationHistoryStore`, `LearningProgressStore`, `LearningActivityStore`, `AppRouteStore`) are constructed in `SwiftMandarinApp.swift` and injected via `.environment(...)`; **`AIModelSettings.shared` is NOT injected** — it is reached as a singleton inside views, an inconsistency to preserve.

Four functional pillars matter here:
- **OCR/Vision** — `PhotoTextRecognitionService` (one `VNRecognizeTextRequest`), fed by 3 independent recognition paths (photo picker, live `DataScannerViewController` camera, screenshot stitch).
- **Language detection/routing** — fragmented across **3+ duplicated detectors** (`PhotoTranslateView.detectLanguage`, `ChineseTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, `EnglishTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, plus naive `containsChinese` scans in `TranslateView`/`LiveSpeechTranslationView`). The only character-level CJK primitive is `Character.isChineseCharacter` (`ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:184`).
- **AI/LLM** — `AIProvider` enum (**2 cases only**) + `AIModelSettings` (Ollama-shaped config) → `AIWordExplanationService` (the dispatch switch) → `OllamaService` (the only network client, wrapping third-party `Ollama.Client`).
- **Translation** — Apple Translation framework (`TranslationSession`) hardcoded to `en` ↔ `zh-Hans`, plus per-word `WordTranslationService`.

App Intents/Shortcuts wrap these via stable singleton signatures and must not be broken by refactors.

---

## 2. CONCERN A — Photo gibberish + stuck on English (VERIFIED root cause)

### Root-cause hypothesis (confirmed by reading the source)
A **compounding 4-stage failure**, all upstream-to-downstream reinforcing "English":

1. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:204`** — `request.recognitionLanguages = ["en-US", "en-GB", "zh-Hans", "zh-Hant"]` with English **first**, and `request.automaticallyDetectsLanguage` is **never set**. On `VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision3` (line 211), supplying an explicit `recognitionLanguages` array suppresses auto-detection and treats the order as a strong prior. There is **no per-call parameter** — the literal is fixed, so the feature genuinely "cannot switch languages."
2. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:207`** — `usesLanguageCorrection = true` unconditionally. English autocorrection mangles Chinese glyphs into Latin-looking gibberish.
3. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:45-72`** (and duplicated at `PhotoTranslateView.swift:601-621`, `CameraScannerView.swift:123-143`) — `cleanTextForSentences` is English-centric: collapses all whitespace to single spaces, strips `"- "`, inserts spaces around `[A-Z]` after `.?!`. Damaging for spaceless full-width-punctuation Chinese.
4. **`PhotoTranslateView.swift:573-598`** — `detectLanguage` runs **after** OCR on already-English-biased text. The CJK-ratio fallback (`chineseCharCount > text.count/3`, line 593) only fires in the `default` branch, so when `NLLanguageRecognizer` confidently returns `.english`, it never runs. `.unknown`/non-Chinese **falls back to English** (lines 561-568, 596). `TextRecognitionResult.language` is hardwired `nil` (line 40), so detected language is never carried downstream.

Secondary: `CameraScannerView.swift:39-47` uses `.text()` with **no** language hint (2nd locked path); `VNImageRequestHandler(cgImage:options:[:])` at line 214 ignores EXIF orientation.

### Exact files / lines / APIs to change
- **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.performRecognition` (lines 200-214)** — make `recognitionLanguages` and `usesLanguageCorrection` **parameters** of `recognizeText(...)`. Best fix: run a cheap detection pass (low-cost OCR or `NLLanguageRecognizer` over a fast first pass), then re-OCR with the detected language **first** (`["zh-Hans","zh-Hant","en-US"]` for Chinese), and set `usesLanguageCorrection = false` for CJK. Pass image **orientation** into `VNImageRequestHandler` (line 214).
- **Populate `TextRecognitionResult.language` (line 40)** so detection result flows downstream.
- **Consolidate the 3 detectors** into one shared function (extend `ChineseTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, `ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:60`) that checks `Character.isChineseCharacter` **ratio first** (the helper already exists at line 184), then consults `NLLanguageRecognizer`. Repoint `PhotoTranslateView.detectLanguage` (573), `ShortcutHelpers.resolveDirection` (34), and `EnglishTextAnalyzer.isEnglish` (405) at it. Remove the English-default fallback in `PhotoTranslateView` (561-568, 596).
- **Skip English cleaners for Chinese** — branch `cleanTextForSentences`/`cleanTextForProcessing` on detected language.
- **`CameraScannerView.swift:40`** — use `.text(languages:)` with the selected/detected language array.
- Widen `Character.isChineseCharacter` (line 184) to include CJK Compatibility Ideographs (0xF900-0xFAFF) and full-width punctuation.

A UI affordance (manual language override in `PhotoTranslateView`'s toolbar `Menu`, lines 102-120) should accompany the auto-detect so the user can force Chinese.

## 3. CONCERN B — Multi-provider AI with API-fetched model lists

### Current abstraction (verified)
- **`AIProvider`** (`AIModelSettings.swift:15-47`): closed 2-case enum (`.appleIntelligence="apple"`, `.ollama="ollama"`), `CaseIterable` — both Settings pickers `ForEach(AIProvider.allCases)` auto-render new cases.
- **`AIModelSettings`** (`AIModelSettings.swift:54-213`): Ollama-shaped fields only (`ollamaModel`, `ollamaHost`, `enableThinking`, `contextLength`), UserDefaults Keys (60-66). **No `apiKey` field, no Keychain anywhere in the codebase.** `effectiveProvider` (123-130) and `statusMessage` (133-152) are exhaustive 2-case switches. `ollamaOptions` (155-163) returns `[String: Ollama.Value]` — SDK-coupled.

# SwiftMandarin — Implementation Brief: OCR Language Fix, Multi-Provider AI, Photo AI Cleanup

## 1. Overall Architecture

SwiftMandarin is a cross-platform (iOS + macOS) SwiftUI Mandarin-learning app. State lives in **`@Observable @MainActor` singletons** (`.shared`) backed by **UserDefaults JSON blobs** — there is no SwiftData/CoreData in active use (`Item.swift` is a dead template stub). The five core stores (`SavedTermsStore`, `TranslationHistoryStore`, `LearningProgressStore`, `LearningActivityStore`, `AppRouteStore`) are constructed in `SwiftMandarinApp.swift` and injected via `.environment(...)`; **`AIModelSettings.shared` is NOT injected** — it is reached as a singleton inside views, an inconsistency to preserve.

Four functional pillars matter here:
- **OCR/Vision** — `PhotoTextRecognitionService` (one `VNRecognizeTextRequest`), fed by 3 independent recognition paths (photo picker, live `DataScannerViewController` camera, screenshot stitch).
- **Language detection/routing** — fragmented across **3+ duplicated detectors** (`PhotoTranslateView.detectLanguage`, `ChineseTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, `EnglishTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, plus naive `containsChinese` scans in `TranslateView`/`LiveSpeechTranslationView`). The only character-level CJK primitive is `Character.isChineseCharacter` (`ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:184`).
- **AI/LLM** — `AIProvider` enum (**2 cases only**) + `AIModelSettings` (Ollama-shaped config) → `AIWordExplanationService` (the dispatch switch) → `OllamaService` (the only network client, wrapping third-party `Ollama.Client`).
- **Translation** — Apple Translation framework (`TranslationSession`) hardcoded to `en` ↔ `zh-Hans`, plus per-word `WordTranslationService`.

App Intents/Shortcuts wrap these via stable singleton signatures and must not be broken by refactors.

## 2. CONCERN A — Photo gibberish + stuck on English (VERIFIED root cause)

### Root-cause hypothesis (confirmed by reading the source)
A **compounding 4-stage failure**, all upstream-to-downstream reinforcing "English":

1. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:204`** — `request.recognitionLanguages = ["en-US", "en-GB", "zh-Hans", "zh-Hant"]` with English **first**, and `request.automaticallyDetectsLanguage` is **never set**. On `VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision3` (line 211), supplying an explicit `recognitionLanguages` array suppresses auto-detection and treats the order as a strong prior. There is **no per-call parameter** — the literal is fixed, so the feature genuinely "cannot switch languages."
2. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:207`** — `usesLanguageCorrection = true` unconditionally. English autocorrection mangles Chinese glyphs into Latin-looking gibberish.
3. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:45-72`** (and duplicated at `PhotoTranslateView.swift:601-621`, `CameraScannerView.swift:123-143`) — `cleanTextForSentences` is English-centric: collapses all whitespace to single spaces, strips `"- "`, inserts spaces around `[A-Z]` after `.?!`. Damaging for spaceless full-width-punctuation Chinese.
4. **`PhotoTranslateView.swift:573-598`** — `detectLanguage` runs **after** OCR on already-English-biased text. The CJK-ratio fallback (`chineseCharCount > text.count/3`, line 593) only fires in the `default` branch, so when `NLLanguageRecognizer` confidently returns `.english`, it never runs. `.unknown`/non-Chinese **falls back to English** (lines 561-568, 596). `TextRecognitionResult.language` is hardwired `nil` (line 40), so detected language is never carried downstream.

Secondary: `CameraScannerView.swift:39-47` uses `.text()` with **no** language hint (2nd locked path); `VNImageRequestHandler(cgImage:options:[:])` at line 214 ignores EXIF orientation.

### Exact files / lines / APIs to change
- **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.performRecognition` (lines 200-214)** — make `recognitionLanguages` and `usesLanguageCorrection` **parameters** of `recognizeText(...)`. Best fix: run a cheap detection pass (low-cost OCR or `NLLanguageRecognizer` over a fast first pass), then re-OCR with the detected language **first** (`["zh-Hans","zh-Hant","en-US"]` for Chinese), and set `usesLanguageCorrection = false` for CJK. # SwiftMandarin — Implementation Brief: OCR Language Fix, Multi-Provider AI, Photo AI Cleanup

## 1. Overall Architecture

SwiftMandarin is a cross-platform (iOS + macOS) SwiftUI Mandarin-learning app. State lives in **`@Observable @MainActor` singletons** (`.shared`) backed by **UserDefaults JSON blobs** — there is no SwiftData/CoreData in active use (`Item.swift` is a dead template stub). The five core stores (`SavedTermsStore`, `TranslationHistoryStore`, `LearningProgressStore`, `LearningActivityStore`, `AppRouteStore`) are constructed in `SwiftMandarinApp.swift` and injected via `.environment(...)`; **`AIModelSettings.shared` is NOT injected** — it is reached as a singleton inside views, an inconsistency to preserve.

Four functional pillars matter here:
- **OCR/Vision** — `PhotoTextRecognitionService` (one `VNRecognizeTextRequest`), fed by 3 independent recognition paths (photo picker, live `DataScannerViewController` camera, screenshot stitch).
- **Language detection/routing** — fragmented across **3+ duplicated detectors** (`PhotoTranslateView.detectLanguage`, `ChineseTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, `EnglishTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, plus naive `containsChinese` scans in `TranslateView`/`LiveSpeechTranslationView`). The only character-level CJK primitive is `Character.isChineseCharacter` (`ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:184`).
- **AI/LLM** — `AIProvider` enum (**2 cases only**) + `AIModelSettings` (Ollama-shaped config) → `AIWordExplanationService` (the dispatch switch) → `OllamaService` (the only network client, wrapping third-party `Ollama.Client`).
- **Translation** — Apple Translation framework (`TranslationSession`) hardcoded to `en` ↔ `zh-Hans`, plus per-word `WordTranslationService`.

App Intents/Shortcuts wrap these via stable singleton signatures and must not be broken by refactors.

## 2. CONCERN A — Photo gibberish + stuck on English (VERIFIED root cause)

### Root-cause hypothesis (confirmed by reading the source)
A **compounding 4-stage failure**, all upstream-to-downstream reinforcing "English":

1. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:204`** — `request.recognitionLanguages = ["en-US", "en-GB", "zh-Hans", "zh-Hant"]` with English **first**, and `request.automaticallyDetectsLanguage` is **never set**. On `VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision3` (line 211), supplying an explicit `recognitionLanguages` array suppresses auto-detection and treats the order as a strong prior. There is **no per-call parameter** — the literal is fixed, so the feature genuinely "cannot switch languages."
2. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:207`** — `usesLanguageCorrection = true` unconditionally. English autocorrection mangles Chinese glyphs into Latin-looking gibberish.
3. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:45-72`** (and duplicated at `PhotoTranslateView.swift:601-621`, `CameraScannerView.swift:123-143`) — `cleanTextForSentences` is English-centric: collapses all whitespace to single spaces, strips `"- "`, inserts spaces around `[A-Z]` after `.?!`. Damaging for spaceless full-width-punctuation Chinese.
4. **`PhotoTranslateView.swift:573-598`** — `detectLanguage` runs **after** OCR on already-English-biased text. The CJK-ratio fallback (`chineseCharCount > text.count/3`, line 593) only fires in the `default` branch, so when `NLLanguageRecognizer` confidently returns `.english`, it never runs. `.unknown`/non-Chinese **falls back to English** (lines 561-568, 596). `TextRecognitionResult.language` is hardwired `nil` (line 40), so detected language is never carried downstream.

Secondary: `CameraScannerView.swift:39-47` uses `.text()` with **no** language hint (2nd locked path); `VNImageRequestHandler(cgImage:options:[:])` at line 214 ignores EXIF orientation.

### Exact files / lines / APIs to change
- **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.performRecognition` (lines 200-214)** — make `recognitionLanguages` and `usesLanguageCorrection` **parameters** of `recognizeText(...)`. Best fix: run a cheap detection pass (low-cost OCR or `NLLanguageRecognizer` over a fast first pass), then re-OCR with the detected language **first** (`["zh-Hans","zh-Hant","en-US"]` for Chinese), and set `usesLanguageCorrection = false` for CJK. Pass image **orientation** into `VNImageRequestHandler` (line 214).
- **Populate `TextRecognitionResult.language` (line 40)** so detection result flows downstream.
- **Consolidate the 3 detectors** into one shared function (extend `ChineseTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, `ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:60`) that checks `Character.isChineseCharacter` **ratio first** (the helper already exists at line 184), then consults `NLLanguageRecognizer`. Repoint `PhotoTranslateView.detectLanguage` (573), `ShortcutHelpers.resolveDirection` (34), and `EnglishTextAnalyzer.isEnglish` (405) at it. Remove the English-default fallback in `PhotoTranslateView` (561-568, 596).
- **Skip English cleaners for Chinese** — branch `cleanTextForSentences`/`cleanTextForProcessing` on detected language.
- **`CameraScannerView.swift:40`** — use `.text(languages:)` with the selected/detected language array.
- Widen `Character.isChineseCharacter` (line 184) to include CJK Compatibility Ideographs (0xF900-0xFAFF) and full-width punctuation.

A UI affordance (manual language override in `PhotoTranslateView`'s toolbar `Menu`, lines 102-120) should accompany the auto-detect so the user can force Chinese.

## 4. CONCERN C — Photo AI cleanup toggle (depends on B's plumbing)

### Exact integration seam
**Primary (single-image path):** `PhotoTranslateView.loadAndProcessImage()` — between `recognizeText(from: data)` (**line 508**) and `sourceText = result.cleanedText` (**line 512**). When the toggle is ON, route `result.fullText` (or, for vision-capable providers, the raw `data`/image) to the selected provider's cleanup method, then substitute the cleaned/structured text before `processText()`.

**Secondary (screenshot path):** `ScreenshotTranslationStore.processScreenshots()` — the `recognizeText(in: stitched.image)` call (`ScreenshotTranslationStore.swift:172`) can branch to a vision model that takes the stitched `UIImage`/`NSImage` directly and returns structured text, skipping Vision OCR entirely. Because `TranslateScreenshotsIntent` hands all images through `ScreenshotTranslationStore.shared`, **no intent-layer change is needed** if cleanup is injected inside the store.

# SwiftMandarin — Implementation Brief: OCR Language Fix, Multi-Provider AI, Photo AI Cleanup

## 1. Overall Architecture

SwiftMandarin is a cross-platform (iOS + macOS) SwiftUI Mandarin-learning app. State lives in **`@Observable @MainActor` singletons** (`.shared`) backed by **UserDefaults JSON blobs** — there is no SwiftData/CoreData in active use (`Item.swift` is a dead template stub). The five core stores (`SavedTermsStore`, `TranslationHistoryStore`, `LearningProgressStore`, `LearningActivityStore`, `AppRouteStore`) are constructed in `SwiftMandarinApp.swift` and injected via `.environment(...)`; **`AIModelSettings.shared` is NOT injected** — it is reached as a singleton inside views, an inconsistency to preserve.

Four functional pillars matter here:
- **OCR/Vision** — `PhotoTextRecognitionService` (one `VNRecognizeTextRequest`), fed by 3 independent recognition paths (photo picker, live `DataScannerViewController` camera, screenshot stitch).
- **Language detection/routing** — fragmented across **3+ duplicated detectors** (`PhotoTranslateView.detectLanguage`, `ChineseTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, `EnglishTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, plus naive `containsChinese` scans in `TranslateView`/`LiveSpeechTranslationView`). The only character-level CJK primitive is `Character.isChineseCharacter` (`ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:184`).
- **AI/LLM** — `AIProvider` enum (**2 cases only**) + `AIModelSettings` (Ollama-shaped config) → `AIWordExplanationService` (the dispatch switch) → `OllamaService` (the only network client, wrapping third-party `Ollama.Client`).
- **Translation** — Apple Translation framework (`TranslationSession`) hardcoded to `en` ↔ `zh-Hans`, plus per-word `WordTranslationService`.

App Intents/Shortcuts wrap these via stable singleton signatures and must not be broken by refactors.

---

## 2. CONCERN A — Photo gibberish + stuck on English (VERIFIED root cause)

### Root-cause hypothesis (confirmed by reading the source)
A **compounding 4-stage failure**, all upstream-to-downstream reinforcing "English":

1. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:204`** — `request.recognitionLanguages = ["en-US", "en-GB", "zh-Hans", "zh-Hant"]` with English **first**, and `request.automaticallyDetectsLanguage` is **never set**. On `VNRecognizeTextRequestRevision3` (line 211), supplying an explicit `recognitionLanguages` array suppresses auto-detection and treats the order as a strong prior. There is **no per-call parameter** — the literal is fixed, so the feature genuinely "cannot switch languages."
2. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:207`** — `usesLanguageCorrection = true` unconditionally. English autocorrection mangles Chinese glyphs into Latin-looking gibberish.
3. **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:45-72`** (and duplicated at `PhotoTranslateView.swift:601-621`, `CameraScannerView.swift:123-143`) — `cleanTextForSentences` is English-centric: collapses all whitespace to single spaces, strips `"- "`, inserts spaces around `[A-Z]` after `.?!`. Damaging for spaceless full-width-punctuation Chinese.
4. **`PhotoTranslateView.swift:573-598`** — `detectLanguage` runs **after** OCR on already-English-biased text. The CJK-ratio fallback (`chineseCharCount > text.count/3`, line 593) only fires in the `default` branch, so when `NLLanguageRecognizer` confidently returns `.english`, it never runs. `.unknown`/non-Chinese **falls back to English** (lines 561-568, 596). `TextRecognitionResult.language` is hardwired `nil` (line 40), so detected language is never carried downstream.

Secondary: `CameraScannerView.swift:39-47` uses `.text()` with **no** language hint (2nd locked path); `VNImageRequestHandler(cgImage:options:[:])` at line 214 ignores EXIF orientation.

### Exact files / lines / APIs to change
- **`PhotoTextRecognitionService.performRecognition` (lines 200-214)** — make `recognitionLanguages` and `usesLanguageCorrection` **parameters** of `recognizeText(...)`. Best fix: run a cheap detection pass (low-cost OCR or `NLLanguageRecognizer` over a fast first pass), then re-OCR with the detected language **first** (`["zh-Hans","zh-Hant","en-US"]` for Chinese), and set `usesLanguageCorrection = false` for CJK. Pass image **orientation** into `VNImageRequestHandler` (line 214).
- **Populate `TextRecognitionResult.language` (line 40)** so detection result flows downstream.
- **Consolidate the 3 detectors** into one shared function (extend `ChineseTextAnalyzer.detectLanguage`, `ChineseTextAnalyzer.swift:60`) that checks `Character.isChineseCharacter` **ratio first** (the helper already exists at line 184), then consults `NLLanguageRecognizer`. Repoint `PhotoTranslateView.detectLanguage` (573), `ShortcutHelpers.resolveDirection` (34), and `EnglishTextAnalyzer.isEnglish` (405) at it. Remove the English-default fallback in `PhotoTranslateView` (561-568, 596).
- **Skip English cleaners for Chinese** — branch `cleanTextForSentences`/`cleanTextForProcessing` on detected language.
- **`CameraScannerView.swift:40`** — use `.text(languages:)` with the selected/detected language array.
- Widen `Character.isChineseCharacter` (line 184) to include CJK Compatibility Ideographs (0xF900-0xFAFF) and full-width punctuation.

A UI affordance (manual language override in `PhotoTranslateView`'s toolbar `Menu`, lines 102-120) should accompany the auto-detect so the user can force Chinese.

---

## 3. CONCERN B — Multi-provider AI with API-fetched model lists

### Current abstraction (verified)
- **`AIProvider`** (`AIModelSettings.swift:15-47`): closed 2-case enum (`.appleIntelligence="apple"`, `.ollama="ollama"`), `CaseIterable` — both Settings pickers `ForEach(AIProvider.allCases)` auto-render new cases.
- **`AIModelSettings`** (`AIModelSettings.swift:54-213`): Ollama-shaped fields only (`ollamaModel`, `ollamaHost`, `enableThinking`, `contextLength`), UserDefaults Keys (60-66). **No `apiKey` field, no Keychain anywhere in the codebase.** `effectiveProvider` (123-130) and `statusMessage` (133-152) are exhaustive 2-case switches. `ollamaOptions` (155-163) returns `[String: Ollama.Value]` — SDK-coupled.
- **`OllamaService`** — the only network client; `refreshModels()` (110-152) is the existing "pull model list from API" pattern (`client.listModels()` + per-model `showModel` capability probe). **Blocker:** the third-party `Ollama.Client` init takes only `(session, host, userAgent)`, `createRequest()` hardcodes `/api/*` paths and sets **no Authorization header** — it **cannot** reach cloud APIs.
- **`AIWordExplanationService`** — dispatch chokepoint: `generateExplanationWithProvider` (388-401) and `translateWithProvider` (408-417) are 2-case switches on `settings.effectiveProvider`. `OllamaWordExplanationResponse` decode is strict (no markdown-fence tolerance).
- **`ShortcutHelpers.aiIsAvailable()` (95)** and `AIWordExplanationView.isAnyProviderAvailable (27)** also hardcode `Apple || Ollama`.

### Concrete plan
1. **Extend `AIProvider`** with `.openAI`, `.anthropic`, `.deepseek`, `.doubao`, `.qwen`, `.kimi`, `.zhipu`, `.minimax`. Add `displayName`/`description`/`iconName`/`defaultBaseURL` per case. Most are **OpenAI-compatible** (`/v1/chat/completions` + `/v1/models`); **Anthropic differs** (`/v1/messages`, `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version` headers).
2. **Introduce a provider protocol** to generalize `OllamaService`'s surface:
   ```swift
   protocol AIProviderClient {
       func listModels() async throws -> [ModelInfo]
       func chatStructured(system: String, user: String, schema: JSONSchema?, image: Data?) async throws -> String
       func translate(_ text: String, sourceIsChinese: Bool) async throws -> String
   }
   ```

63	    private static func translateWithRetry(
64	        _ text: String,
65	        direction: TranslationDirection,
66	        maxRetries: Int
67	    ) async throws -> (translation: String, usedAI: Bool) {
68	        var lastError: Error?
69

72	                // Create a fresh session for each attempt
73	                let session = try await TranslationSession(

75	                    target: direction.targetLanguage

83	                if attempt < maxRetries {

# Handoff.md — SwiftMandarin: Bilingual + Multi-Provider AI Overhaul

**Last Updated (UTC):** 2026-06-04
**Status:** In Progress
**Current Focus:** Four-part overhaul — (A) fix photo OCR Chinese gibberish/language lock, (B) multi-provider cloud AI with API-fetched model lists, (C) photo→AI cleanup toggle, (D) make the app fully bilingual (dual narration + learner-mode toggle).

## 1) Request & Context
- **A — Photo OCR bug:** Photo upload "often produces gibberish," "cannot switch languages," "stuck on detecting English, can't read Mandarin."

# Handoff.md — SwiftMandarin: Bilingual + Multi-Provider AI Overhaul

**Last Updated (UTC):** 2026-06-04
**Status:** In Progress
**Current Focus:** Four-part overhaul — (A) fix photo OCR Chinese gibberish/language lock, (B) multi-provider cloud AI with API-fetched model lists, (C) photo→AI cleanup toggle, (D) make the app fully bilingual (dual narration + learner-mode toggle).

## 1) Request & Context
- **A — Photo OCR bug:** Photo upload "often produces gibberish," "cannot switch languages," "stuck on detecting English, can't read Mandarin."
- **B — Provider expansion:** Add OpenAI, Claude (Anthropic), Deepseek, Doubao, Qwen, Kimi, Zhipu, Minimax. Pull each provider's available models via API.
- **C — Deep AI integration:** A settings toggle that routes an uploaded photo to an AI model for cleanup/structuring, returning cleaned text into the app.
- **D — Bilingual:** App must serve English-speakers-learning-Mandarin AND Mandarin-speakers-learning-English (and both). Add English narration alongside Mandarin for the selected word, and a settings toggle that flips the app between English-centric and Mandarin-centric, adapting features.

**Environment:** Xcode 26.3, iOS/macOS/visionOS **26.2** deploy targets, Swift 5 mode, single target `SwiftMandarin`, sandboxed (`ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX=YES`), generated Info.plist. One SPM dep: `ollama-swift 1.8.0`. State = `@Observable @MainActor` singletons over UserDefaults JSON. No Keychain, no network entitlement yet.

## 2) Verified Root Causes (from full-codebase read + 9-agent comprehension workflow)
**A (compounding 4-stage failure):**
1. `PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift:204` — `recognitionLanguages = ["en-US","en-GB","zh-Hans","zh-Hant"]` English-first; `automaticallyDetectsLanguage` never set; no per-call override → genuinely "cannot switch languages."
2. `:207` — `usesLanguageCorrection = true` unconditionally → English autocorrect mangles Chinese into Latin gibberish.
3. `:45-72` (+ dup in `PhotoTranslateView:601`, `CameraScannerView:123`) — English-centric cleaner joins with spaces / English punctuation regex → corrupts spaceless Chinese.
4. `PhotoTranslateView:573-598` — language detection runs AFTER OCR on already-garbled text; non-Chinese falls back to English; `TextRecognitionResult.language` hardwired `nil`.

---
name: build-and-project-structure
description: How to build SwiftMandarin, its sandbox/network entitlement, and how new Swift files get into the build
metadata:
  type: project
---

SwiftMandarin is a single-target multiplatform SwiftUI app (iOS/macOS/visionOS **26.2** deploy targets, Swift 5 mode, Xcode 26.3). One SPM dependency: `ollama-swift 1.8.0`.

**Build/verify commands (both pass clean):**
- macOS: `xcodebuild -scheme SwiftMandarin -destination 'platform=macOS' -configuration Debug build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`
- iOS: `xcodebuild -scheme SwiftMandarin -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' -configuration Debug build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`

**New Swift files:** the target uses `fileSystemSynchronizedGroups = (SwiftMandarin)`, so any `.swift` file added under `SwiftMandarin/` is auto-included in the build — no `project.pbxproj` editing needed. (There are also ~24 legacy explicit file refs in the pbxproj; leave them, Xcode 26 dedupes by path.)

**Sandbox:** `ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX = YES`. The entitlements file is `SwiftMandarin/SwiftMandarin.entitlements`. Outbound networking (Ollama on macOS, all cloud AI providers) REQUIRES `com.apple.security.network.client` — this was missing and added 2026-06-04. Info.plist is generated (`GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE=YES`) via `INFOPLIST_KEY_*` build settings; note `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`/`NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` are currently empty strings (latent iOS crash risk if speech permission is requested).

State pattern: `@Observable @MainActor` singletons (`.shared`) over UserDefaults JSON; stores injected via `.environment(...)` in `SwiftMandarinApp`, but `AIModelSettings.shared`/`AppPreferences.shared` are reached as singletons inside views. See [[ai-provider-architecture]].

**AI providers** (added 2026-06-04): `AIProvider` enum (`Models/AIModelSettings.swift`) has 10 cases — `appleIntelligence`, `ollama`, and 8 cloud: `openAI, anthropic, deepseek, doubao, qwen, kimi, zhipu, minimax`. Per-provider metadata (baseURL, chatPath, modelsPath, defaultModels, apiStyle, supportsVision, keychainAccount) lives on the enum. Cloud calls go through `Services/CloudAIService.swift` (URLSession; OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` + Anthropic `/v1/messages`; vision via base64 image; `refreshModels` lists via `/models` with curated-default fallback). API keys live in the **Keychain** via `Services/KeychainHelper.swift` (account `apikey.<rawValue>`), mirrored in `AIModelSettings.apiKeys` for SwiftUI reactivity.

**Dispatch chokepoint:** `Services/AIWordExplanationService.swift` — `generateExplanationWithProvider` / `translateWithProvider` switch on `effectiveProvider` with `apple` / `ollama` / `default:` (cloud) cases. `cleanupRecognizedText(_:imageData:hintedLanguage:)` is the photo-AI-cleanup entry. When adding provider behavior, use `default:` cases so new providers don't break exhaustive switches. Settings UI is the shared `Views/Components/AIProviderConfigView.swift` used by both macOS `AISettingsTab` and iOS `AISettingsDetailView`.

**Photo OCR (concern-A fix):** `Services/PhotoTextRecognitionService.swift` recognition language/correction is parameterized via `PhotoScanLanguage` (in `Models/AppPreferences.swift`: auto/chinese/english/bilingual). The root bug was English-first `recognitionLanguages` + `usesLanguageCorrection=true` mangling Chinese. Language detection is now `ChineseTextAnalyzer.detectLanguageRobust` (CJK-ratio-first, beats `NLLanguageRecognizer` on mixed/noisy OCR). Three OCR paths (photo picker, `CameraScannerView` live camera, `ScreenshotTranslationStore`) — keep them consistent. `AppPreferences.learnerMode` (English-centric/Mandarin-centric/bilingual) drives the `defaultDirection` UserDefaults key; `dualNarration` enables both-language speak buttons in word-detail views. See [[build-and-project-structure]].

Concern A (photo OCR gibberish / stuck on English):
- Parameterize Vision recognitionLanguages + usesLanguageCorrection via a new

  first so it is no longer mangled into Latin gibberish.
- Add robust CJK-ratio-first language detection (detectLanguageRobust), widen
  CJK ranges, carry detected language on TextRecognitionResult, honor EXIF
  orientation, and clean Chinese OCR text without English-centric regex.
- Add a scan-language selector + Re-recognize control to the photo screen and
  pass the language hint to the live camera scanner (.text(languages:)).

Concern B (expand AI providers + API-fetched models):
- Extend AIProvider to 10 providers (OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, Doubao, Qwen,
  Kimi, Zhipu, MiniMax + Apple/Ollama) with per-provider REST metadata.
- New CloudAIService (URLSession): OpenAI-compatible + Anthropic chat, vision,
  and model listing with curated-default fallback.
- Store API keys in the Keychain (KeychainHelper); add per-provider key/model/
  base-URL config; generalize availability/status switches.
- Shared AIProviderConfigView wired into macOS + iOS settings.
- Add com.apple.security.network.client entitlement (sandbox needs it for any
  outbound networking, including Ollama on macOS).

Concern C (photo -> AI cleanup toggle):
- aiPhotoCleanupEnabled toggle routes OCR text (and the image, for vision
  providers) through the selected model via cleanupRecognizedText before
  analysis/translation.

Concern D (bilingual):
- AppPreferences.learnerMode (English-centric / Mandarin-centric / bilingual)
  adapts the default translation direction; dual-language narration in the
  word-detail views (Mandarin + English).

Builds clean on macOS and iOS; detector/cleaning logic verified (9/9 checks)."
